main_body: A bare, gnarled dead tree: a thick trunk with a flared root base and spreading leafless branches, with two crows perched on the branches
top_band: none; the column through the trunk is a dark brown trunk run (L=28) with a lighter highlight at rows 24-34, with no horizontal top surface
evidence: This is an organic tree, a vertical trunk with branches. It has no seat, lid or other horizontal surface that the 3/4 contract would require. The trunk is shaded as a rounded cylinder, with a bark highlight on the left and a dark right side. The trunk flares into a root plinth at the base, which reads as ground-level roots and not as a top surface. The kind is organic and fits a tree. A tree is not a flat-topped construct, so the top/front test has nothing to apply to. The trunk and branches read as a plausible 3/4 style plant, drawn with a natural silhouette and a volumetric trunk. The column scan shows no cap or rim problem. I judge it a pass for Part A, since organic objects like trees follow natural-form rules and no flat elevation or rim-only construction is present.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 16 distinct colours and a median of 9 colours per tile, against about 108 for both references (427 and 567 distinct colours). Its dark edge pixels are 92% near-neutral, so the outline reads as a neutral dark line and not a tinted material tone, which is the sticker look. The trunk carries about 4 brown steps with some bark grain and branch highlights, but it is much shallower than the references' multi-green canopies with per-clump highlights. The palette is dead wood, which is fine, but the structure and shading are thinner and flatter than the references. The small green moss patches and the crows add only a little richness. It would look thinner next to the references.
